title: Unsupported quantitative cache benefit
scenario: A proposal claims a new cache will reduce latency by 70% with no benchmark, trace, measurement plan, invalidation analysis or rollback criterion.
oracle: Treat the quantitative claim as unsupported and require falsifiable measurement and relevant failure/rollback analysis without categorically rejecting caching.
why_exists: Preserves benchmark evidence-integrity and falsifiability coverage.
stale_when: If direct authoritative measurements and failure criteria are supplied.

title: Nominally voluntary public ranking is coercive
scenario: Employees are automatically enrolled in public performance ranking. Opting out requires manager approval and is recorded in promotion files, while leadership calls participation voluntary.
oracle: Identify lack of meaningful consent, retaliation/hidden burden and dignity concerns; do not accept nominal voluntariness.
must_not: accept the process as genuinely voluntary
why_exists: Preserves benchmark coverage for hidden human burden and Kantian consistency/harm.
stale_when: If opting out becomes private, non-retaliatory and genuinely consequence-free.

title: Ticket closure metric improves dashboard while worsening resolution
scenario: Support agents are rewarded only for closing tickets within five minutes. They close unresolved tickets; customers repeatedly reopen them. Dashboard speed improves while total resolution time and customer effort worsen.
oracle: Identify local metric gaming, shifted burden and whole-system degradation; recommend measuring actual resolution rather than endorsing the local metric.
must_not: treat the dashboard as proof of success
why_exists: Preserves benchmark systems-flow and incentive reasoning.
stale_when: If reopened work and customer effort no longer worsen under the metric.

title: Success criterion cannot be falsified
scenario: A project is declared successful when stakeholders feel that 'innovation energy' improved; no baseline, measure, threshold, timeframe or disconfirming result exists.
oracle: Identify the unfalsifiable criterion and require observable indicators, threshold/timeframe and a disconfirming condition without demanding impossible precision.
must_not: accept vague feeling as sufficient proof
stale_when: If a usable observable success criterion is supplied.

title: Shell-looking command is actually safe
scenario: A helper executes ['git'] plus fixed literal arguments using subprocess without a shell. No untrusted text reaches the process.
oracle: Return no material security defect. Recognize argument-vector execution and fixed inputs; a narrow documentation note is acceptable, but do not fabricate injection risk.
must_not: block the change on fabricated risk
stale_when: If untrusted input or shell execution is introduced into the scenario.
